question: In which year was the Dutch East India Company (Vereenigde Oostindische Compagnie - VOC) formed through the amalgamation of several rival trading companies?
explanation: The Dutch East India Company (VOC) was established on March 20, 1602, when the States-General of the Netherlands granted it a 21-year monopoly to carry out trade activities in Asia. This consolidated the rival pre-companies (Voorcompagnieën) into a single powerful entity.

question: Which governing body in the Netherlands granted the charter to the Dutch East India Company (VOC), empowering it to wage war, conclude treaties, and construct fortresses?
explanation: The States-General of the Netherlands (the sovereign parliament of the Dutch Republic) granted the VOC a charter which gave it quasi-governmental powers, including the authority to raise armies, build forts, mint coins, and negotiate treaties on behalf of the state.
